description:
We are a multidisciplinary team combining Earth science, signal analysis, and AI to detect and distinguish atmospheric and geological events through integrated infrasound and seismic data.

We welcome passionate contributors with skills in signal processing, geophysics, Python, AI/ML, data analysis, and scientific visualization to help us push this project further.
summary:
SKYQUAKE X is an integrated geophysical analysis platform designed to investigate events that connect Earth's atmosphere and solid ground. It combines atmospheric infrasound and seismic waveform analysis to help distinguish meteor airbursts, earthquakes, and other sources of unusual signals.

Rather than relying on a single sensor or isolated waveform, SKYQUAKE X analyzes complementary observations, examining their timing, signal characteristics, and cross-sensor relationships to build a more reliable interpretation of an event.

The platform aims to reduce ambiguity in geophysical event analysis by connecting evidence from two different physical environments within one unified system. By bringing atmospheric and seismic observations together, SKYQUAKE X offers a new perspective on how events can be detected, compared, and investigated.

Our goal is to support more informed scientific analysis of atmospheric and seismic phenomena through multimodal data integration, signal processing, and evidence-based event classification.
details:
SKYQUAKE X approaches atmospheric and seismic event detection as one connected scientific problem.

The central idea is that different physical events can produce signals that appear similar when examined independently. A single waveform may not provide enough evidence to determine whether an event originated in the atmosphere, within the Earth's crust, or from another source.

To address this limitation, SKYQUAKE X brings together two complementary observation types:

1. Atmospheric Infrasound Analysis

The platform examines low-frequency acoustic signals generated by atmospheric phenomena, including potential meteor airbursts. It considers signal characteristics, temporal patterns, and noise conditions.

2. Seismic Waveform Analysis

It examines ground-motion signals to identify seismic activity and other events that may produce measurable disturbances in the Earth's surface.

3. Cross-Sensor Correlation

Instead of treating each signal as an independent observation, SKYQUAKE X investigates temporal alignment and relationships between atmospheric and seismic measurements. This helps determine whether different observations may be associated with the same event.

4. Evidence-Based Event Classification

The platform combines signal characteristics and available observations to support the differentiation of meteor-related events, earthquakes, and background noise. Its objective is to support scientific investigation rather than present an uncertain classification as a confirmed discovery.

Technical Approach

The project incorporates waveform visualization, signal processing, time-frequency analysis, sensor integration, and event correlation. Its development combines Python-based data processing and web technologies for presenting observations through an integrated monitoring interface.

Innovation and Impact

The main innovation is not simply detecting an unusual signal, but investigating the relationship between signals recorded in two different physical environments.

SKYQUAKE X aims to make geophysical observations more connected, interpretable, and useful for further scientific investigation. By bringing atmospheric and seismic evidence together, it provides a framework for exploring events that cannot be fully understood through one observation channel alone.
